memory_update.text: AI theme should be researched as an infrastructure stack: compute demand creates bottlenecks in bandwidth, memory, advanced packaging, optical interconnects, power, cooling, grid access, and firm power.
Optical interconnect materials, InP/III-V photonics, photodetectors, and 800G/1.6T transceiver manufacturing are high-priority underfollowed AI supply-chain lanes.
HBM and advanced packaging demand may create OSAT overflow opportunities in memory backend, fan-out panel-level packaging, test, and co-packaged optics.

Data-center power and thermal balance-of-plant should be decomposed beyond Vertiv/Eaton into smaller suppliers of switchgear, transformers, busway, UPS, CDUs, cold plates, connectors, and commissioning services.
Firm power and grid constraints link AI data-center growth to nuclear fuel, reactor components, transmission construction, engineering, interconnection, and permitting bottlenecks.

Next layer should verify all company-specific claims using primary filings, earnings calls, backlog/capex disclosures, customer qualification evidence, market cap, analyst coverage, and valuation/pricing checks.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposes the broad AI theme into a supply-chain funnel rather than a ticker list. The strongest decomposition lanes are: AI compute demand driving bandwidth and memory pressure; hyperscaler capex shifting bottlenecks from GPUs into optical interconnects, advanced packaging, power, cooling, grid access, and nuclear or firm power; and enterprise AI automation creating second-order software/data infrastructure demand. For underfollowed discovery, the highest-quality starting points are narrow suppliers with qualification cycles, constrained process know-how, customer concentration, substrate/device capacity limits, testing/packaging bottlenecks, and power-infrastructure permitting or interconnection delays. This is an initial theme-map layer only, not a buy/sell recommendation.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders such as NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, Constellation, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta only to identify where capex and bottlenecks are moving. Lane 2 searches for underfollowed suppliers one or two steps upstream or downstream: optical substrates, photonic-device manufacturing, transceiver contract manufacturing, OSAT overflow, advanced packaging tools/materials, power/cooling subcomponents, grid services, nuclear fuel/components, and vertical AI automation vendors. Candidate quality should be judged by evidence of customer qualification, capacity allocation, backlog, pricing power, margin inflection, revenue mix shift, capex expansion, and dependency on unavoidable system constraints.
supply_side_constraints: Commercial qualification cycles for optical and precision substrate suppliers can be long, creating delayed supply response.
Indium phosphide and related compound-semiconductor device capacity may be constrained despite fab expansions, according to supplied search context.
HBM and advanced packaging priority can crowd out conventional memory backend capacity, pushing overflow toward outsourced packaging and test providers.
AI data centers face power availability, grid interconnection, permitting, cooling, and equipment lead-time constraints.
Nuclear and firm-power solutions face licensing, construction, fuel availability, regulatory, and project execution constraints.
AI software monetization faces integration complexity, data quality limits, security requirements, procurement friction, and uncertain ROI.
